subject: Commercial furniture built around brand and workflow
hook: Before choosing a reception desk colour, map the visitor's first 30 seconds
ig:
Before choosing a reception desk colour, map what happens in the first 30 seconds after a visitor walks in.

Commercial furniture works when it is designed around workflow first and branding second. For a reception desk, that means answering a few questions early:

Can staff see the door without turning round?
Is there a lower section so a seated visitor or wheelchair user can be served face to face?
Where do parcels and post go, out of the visitor's sight?
What needs power: screens, card readers, phones, printers?
Where does your brand show, and which edges take the knocks?

Get those right and the finish becomes the easy part. We design and build reception desks and office storage in our own workshop in Stoke-on-Trent.

Save this for your next fit-out, and find our commercial work via the link in bio.
fb:
Running a salon, clinic, office or showroom and thinking about a new reception desk? Start with how people move, not with colour swatches.

Where do visitors walk in? Can whoever's on the desk see them? Where do deliveries land? What needs plugging in? Only then does it make sense to choose finishes, often in your brand colours, with hard-wearing edges where bags and chairs knock into it.

We make reception desks and office storage in our workshop in Hanley, Stoke-on-Trent, and fit them with our own team. Have a look at our commercial cabinet making here:
